summary.headline: Apollo Tyres Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 74bn (+12.8% YoY), EBITDA margin 11.7% (down ~150bp) on ~17% raw material inflation.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12.8% YoY to INR 74bn but was flat-ish sequentially, with consolidated EBITDA margin down about 150bp YoY to 11.7% on raw material cost pressure. India delivered its highest-ever revenue of INR 54.6bn (+15.6% YoY, +4.3% QoQ), largely volume-led, with India EBITDA margin at 12% versus 13.6%. Europe revenue was EUR147m (+0.5% YoY) with EBITDA of EUR13m (8.9% margin), hit by Enschede closure transition and agri revenue loss. Management said price increases lag raw material inflation and that most of the catch-up flows into Q2 and H2.

financial_highlights.change: India capex INR 500 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material cost increase in Q1
financial_highlights.change: Rubber INR 225/kg, synthetic INR 250, carbon black INR 125, steel cord INR 165 (as quoted)

segments.name: India operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 54.6bn (+15.6% YoY), double-digit growth across all segments; volume growth Replacement 13%, OEM 10%, Exports 15%. TBB was the only category without double-digit growth. Price increases ~3-4% realised in Q1 versus 7-9% taken.

segments.name: Europe operations
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR147m (+0.5% YoY) and EBITDA EUR13m (8.9%). PCR replacement grew double digits; agri revenue fell high-teens QoQ and small single digits YoY. Without Enschede overlap costs, margin would have been ~11%.

segments.name: Reifen
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR43m in Q1 with ~3% EBITDA margin, as disclosed on the call.

guidance_outlook: Raw material inflation of ~8% sequentially expected in Q2 for India; Europe RM basket up 8% in Q1 with hit mainly in Q2.

India needs ~15-16% total price increase to cover commodity inflation; ~11%+ currently in place (9% TBR, 11% other categories); at least 1-2 more hikes needed; July hike 1-2%, similar hike expected in August.
Europe needs ~10% price increase across Q1-Q2; only 3-4% implemented so far.
Europe full-year EBITDA target: high teens margin once manufacturing footprint transition completes.
Net debt/EBITDA expected to rise slightly this year as company becomes a net borrower; capex to rise in Q2 and Q3.
Rubber expected to cool from Q3 as seasonal impact fades; crude-linked cost relief expected with a quarter lag.
capex_capacity: Enschede (Netherlands) plant stopped production in June 2026; ~750,000 tyres/year shifting largely to Hungary, completion Sept-Oct 2026; financial benefits from H2 FY27.
Hungary PCR capacity rising from ~17,000 to ~21,000 car tyres per day, starting H2 FY27; Hungary expanding by 4,000 PCR tyres/day, AP (India) plant expanding double that.
Lower-end 14-15 inch tyres moving from Hungary to India; Spacemaster spare tyre production now in Baroda; India new capacity to start towards end of FY27 and ramp through FY28.
High-end agri (OHT) capacity limited at Kalamassery (Kochi); no economic small-scale alternative; offtake partner identified near Asia-Europe cusp, midterm plan is offtake.
India capex was ~INR 1,200-1,300 crore annually in recent past; FY27 group capex guided above INR 3,000 crore.
Management says India running in the 90s on capacity utilisation and will stay tight through FY27.
demand_pricing: India replacement momentum strong; July started strongly and Q2 YoY growth expected to be good though QoQ muted due to rains and seasonality.
Europe: anti-dumping duty on Chinese tyres expected to help Apollo brand at lower end; Vredestein PCR does not compete with Chinese.
Exports growth driven by Europe; West Asia impacted by war and US underperformed due to dealer inventory issues.
Competition has broadly followed price increases of similar magnitude, per management.
Management market share estimates (internal): TBR replacement upwards of 30% (regained lost share); PCR replacement 21%+.
UHP mix in Europe stayed at around 40%, per management recollection.
Advertising and sales promotion spend cut by roughly 50% QoQ; management said no further reduction expected.

qa_highlights.question: India volume growth by channel and outlook; Europe anti-dumping and capacity shift timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement +13%, OEM +10%, exports +15% volume growth; Q2 seasonal. Enschede-to-Hungary shift to complete Sept-Oct 2026; Spacemaster already in Baroda.

qa_highlights.question: How much India and Europe price hikes have been taken vs needed?
qa_highlights.answer: India: 7-9% implemented in Q1 (only 3-4% flowed into revenue), 11%+ now against 15-16% needed. Europe: 3-4% implemented against ~10% needed.

qa_highlights.question: Europe margin without overlap costs and steady-state target?
qa_highlights.answer: ~11% margin without overlap; full-year Europe target high-teens EBITDA margin after footprint change.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and net debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 consolidated capex INR 650 crore; India INR 500 crore; capex to step up in Q2-Q3; company to become net borrower with slight rise in net debt/EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses and staff cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P cut ~50% QoQ but no further reduction expected; minor increments effective June 1 with full impact from Q2, no further increment planned.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material outlook: rupee, rubber, crude?
qa_highlights.answer: ~7-8% of RM inflation from rupee depreciation (from INR 88); ~50% of RM imported; domestic rubber ~50-50 mix; rubber expected to cool from Q3; crude relief with a quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive pricing behaviour and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition has followed price increases of similar magnitude; TBR share back above 30%, PCR replacement 21%+ (internal estimates).

risks_watch: Raw material pass-through lag: India needs ~15-16% total price increase versus ~11%+ in place, with at least 1-2 more hikes needed; OEM formula pricing flows with a quarter lag and truck contracts are negotiated.
Europe price gap: only 3-4% implemented against ~10% needed for Q1-Q2, and Europe RM basket up 8% with the hit mainly in Q2.

Europe execution: Enschede-to-Hungary transfer to complete Sept-Oct 2026; high-end agri relies on an unnamed offtake partner, with about 20-25% of agri volume offtaken and a couple of quarters needed to stabilise customer approvals.
Capex and leverage: FY27 group capex guided above INR 3,000 crore, rising in Q2-Q3; company turns net borrower and net debt/EBITDA rises slightly from 0.4x.

Commodity reversal and price correction: rubber expected to cool from Q3 and crude relief with a quarter lag, but management flagged possible price correction in Q4 if RM falls sharply; export weakness in West Asia and US.

So the current quantum of price increase is about 9% in TBR and 11% in other categories.
So I would admit to you that we'll have to get back to you. I can't give you a conclusive answer if there's been a pre-buy.

summary.management_tone: Confident on India demand and pricing momentum (July start strong, capacity running in the 90s), but cautious on Europe margins and near-term raw material costs, which management said remain volatile. Answers were often hedged or deferred, e.g. pre-buy question ("I can't give you a conclusive answer") and debt trajectory, with the outgoing CFO handling the call.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue +12.8% YoY with India +15.6% and utilisation in the 90s, plus Hungary and India capacity coming online from H2 FY27 to FY28; offset by Europe flat at +0.5%, margin pressure from ~17% raw material inflation, and price increases lagging costs.
